UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
DEPARTMENT OF THE TREASURY
FINANCIAL CRIMES ENFORCEMENT NETWORK
IN THE MATTER OF No. 2001 - 02
ANGELINA PLETT
ASSESSMENT OF CIVIL MONEY PENALTIES
AGAINST ANGELINA PLETT
I. INTRODUCTION
The Secretary of the United States Department of the Treasury has delegated to
the Director of the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (“FinCEN”) the authority to
determine whether a financial institution has violated the Bank Secrecy Act, 31 U.S.C.
§§5311 et seq. and 31 CFR Part 103 thereunder (“BSA”), and what, if any, sanction is
appropriate.
II. JURISDICTION
Angelina Plett (“Plett”) was, at all relevant times, an owner and the manager of
Cash For Checks Inc. (“Cash For Checks”). Cash For Checks was, at all relevant times, a
licensed check casher located in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma and was a “financial
institution” within the meaning of 31 U.S.C. §5312(a)(2) and 31 CFR §103.11(n).1
III. FINCEN’S DETERMINATIONS
A. Structuring
FinCEN has determined that between July 11, 1995, and April 26, 1996, Plett
willfully structured or willfully assisted in structuring check cashing transactions for
Joseph A. Sivigliano (“Sivigliano”) through a domestic financial institution in violation
of 31 U.S.C. §5324(a)(3) and 31 CFR §103.63(c). During the relevant time period,
Sivigliano cashed 136 checks totaling more than $1.17 million at Cash For Checks. On
each of 43 days, Sivigliano cashed a series of checks that individually totaled less than
$10,000, but that together exceeded $10,0

4) Sum inbound amounts for AC720644 from transactions[8..11]: 2,205.40 + 7,418.10 + 5,172.84 + 2,607.90 = 17,404.24.
5) Sum inbound amounts for AC691807 from transactions[12..15]: 7,017.31 + 8,179.07 + 6,802.69 + 9,869.77 = 31,868.84.
6) Sum inbound amounts for AC795205 from transactions[16..19]: 4,777.28 + 4,964.20 + 4,729.51 + 8,577.83 = 23,048.82.
7) Sum inbound amounts for AC128418 from transactions[20..23]: 9,685.34 + 8,628.83 + 5,483.46 + 9,722.82 = 33,520.45.
8) Sum inbound amounts for AC188025 from transactions[24..26]: 8,464.79 + 5,867.50 = 14,332.29.
9) Total inbound across distinct sender accounts = 17,912.10 + 27,624.74 + 17,404.24 + 31,868.84 + 23,048.82 + 33,520.45 + 14,332.29 = 147,604.88.

statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5324?
statutory.answer: Neutral: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring, but the facts do not show cash transactions structured to evade a CTR reporting requirement (e.g., breaking up >$10,000 cash transactions on the same day) or intent to evade reporting.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring (and related conduct) for the purpose of evading Bank Secrecy Act reporting requirements, including causing or attempting to cause a domestic financial institution to fail to file a required report (e.g., a CTR) or structuring/assisting in structuring transactions to evade such reporting. Here, the fact pattern shows multiple inbound transactions labeled “smurfing fan-in deposit,” including several cash deposits (e.g., $3,594.69, $3,218.91, $7,355.00, $8,134.42, $9,716.80, etc.) and several ACH credits. However, § 5324’s core element is purpose/intent to evade a reporting requirement tied to reportable transactions (typically CTRs for cash transactions over $10,000 in a single business day). The record does not state whether any cash deposits were made at/through a domestic financial institution in a manner that would otherwise trigger a CTR, whether multiple cash deposits on the same day were by/for the same person such that they should be aggregated above $10,000, or any evidence of intent to evade (e.g., instructions to keep deposits under $10,000, teller interactions, prior CTR filings, or explicit evasion behavior). Additionally, several transactions are ACH, which generally are not CTR-triggering cash transactions. Because the facts do not establish (1) a reportable cash transaction that was broken up/structured, and (2) the purpose of evading reporting, it cannot be determined that 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring as applied to these facts.
